jurisdiction.name: Tonga
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Tonga has no AI strategy or AI-specific law. AI is covered by two 2025 Acts: the Computer Crimes Act, in force since October 2025, which defines AI and deepfakes and criminalises harmful electronic communications including intimate recordings made with generative AI; and the Privacy Act, enacted in December 2025 but not yet in force, which gives a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and a right to object to profiling.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the Attorney General's Office legislation portal and the official gazette supplements. The digital transformation department's, the ministry's (MEIDECC) and the Prime Minister's Office websites could not be accessed, so any AI policy published only there could not be checked. Tonga is marked for a later retry. The digital government framework and AI policy work are tracked as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Legislative Assembly of Tonga; assented to by King Tupou VI
instruments.summary: Tonga's first general data protection law: it sets lawful bases and requirements for processing personal information by data controllers and processors (including the State), breach notification, personal information protection impact assessments and rules on transfers outside the Kingdom, and creates a Privacy Commission headed by a Privacy Commissioner with enforcement notices and pecuniary penalties. Section 44 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless it is necessary for a contract, authorised by a written law with safeguards, or consented to; section 45 adds a right to object to processing, including profiling.
instruments.current_status: Act 34 of 2025, assented to by King Tupou VI on 16 December 2025 and issued with Tonga Government Gazette Supplement Extraordinary No.17 of 17 December 2025. Section 1(2): comes into force on a date proclaimed by Cabinet. No commencement proclamation was found in the Gazette Supplements Extraordinary through No.05 of 2026 or in the commencement notes of the Attorney General's Office acts-by-year listing (checked 2026-10-13), so it is treated as enacted but not yet in force. A Tongan-language version (Lao ki he Totonu ki he Meʻa Fakafoʻituitui 2025) is published alongside.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Act PDF read with pdftotext (assent, s.1 commencement, ss.38, 44, 45); Gazette Supplement Extraordinary No.17/2025 read for issue date; 2026 Gazette Supplements Extraordinary 01-05 and ago.gov.to acts-by-year 2025 commencement notes checked for a proclamation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law with an explicit right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, including profiling; governs AI use of personal information.

instruments.issuing_authority: Legislative Assembly of Tonga; assented to by King Tupou VI
instruments.summary: Criminal law on computer-related offences and investigative powers (search warrants, preservation and production of computer data). Section 18 defines 'AI' and 'deep fake' (visual or audio content generated or manipulated using AI that misrepresents someone or something) and makes it an offence to use a service to post a menacing, harassing or harmful electronic communication, expressly including intimate recordings created with generative AI deepfakes. Posting such an intimate recording is punishable by a fine of up to TOP 50,000, up to 7 years' imprisonment, or both.
instruments.current_status: Act 15 of 2025, assented to by King Tupou VI on 28 August 2025 and issued with Tonga Government Gazette Supplement Extraordinary No.10 of 4 September 2025. In force since 1 October 2025 by Cabinet proclamation under section 1(2), published in Gazette Supplement Extraordinary No.12 of 1 October 2025.

instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Creates an AI deepfake-related offence: defines AI and deep fakes and criminalises posting harmful AI-generated intimate recordings.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Tonga's legislation portal (acts, bills and gazette supplements), Parliament, the government portal, ministries and regulators were searched in English and Tongan. Apart from the Privacy Act 2025 and the Computer Crimes Act 2025, no qualifying AI-governance document was found. The Digital Transformation Department, the ministry responsible for communications (MEIDECC) and the Prime Minister's Office sites were unavailable, so any AI policy published only there still needs to be checked.
